title: Kingdom of Thessalonica
capsule: The Kingdom of Thessalonica was a short-lived Crusader state carved out of the Byzantine Empire after the Fourth Crusade's sack of Constantinople in 1204, granted to the Montferrat marquis Boniface I, who was crowned king that year. It was formally a vassal of the Latin Empire of Constantinople and covered much of Macedonian and Thessalian Greece. Following Boniface's death in a Bulgarian ambush in 1207, the kingdom was progressively weakened; the ruler Demetrios of Montferrat ceded it to the restored Epirote ruler Theodore Komnenos Doukas, who conquered Thessalonica in 1224 and extinguished the Latin kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's general extent across Macedonia and Thessaly is established from Latin chronicles and Villehardouin's account; exact frontier lines in the uplands of Epirus are uncertain due to the rapid political fragmentation of 1204–1224.
